gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Sony XAV-AX6000 only gives climate control, gauges, vehicle info (tire pressure, battery voltage) and Park Assist on its screen after you buy a separate iDatalink Maestro module and flash it at idatalinkmaestro.com with your car type and the receiver's serial number, and that Sony says the functions you get depend on your car and the firmware.
standout_why: CarAudioNow's buyer's guide (cited by ChatGPT) already marks the XAV-AX6000, XAV-9000ES, DMX958XR and DMH-WT6000NEX as 'Maestro RR/RR2 ready, vehicle dependent'. It says to check factory-amp retention 'by exact application' and that steering controls need 'the correct receiver, interface, and firmware for the exact vehicle'. So the basic mechanism is already in a cited page. What it lacks is what Maestro shows on the Sony screen (climate, gauges, tire pressure, Park Assist), that the module is sold separately, and the step of flashing the module with the vehicle firmware and the receiver's serial number. Truepicked mentions Maestro only for a Kenwood DMX9707S. The visible part of World Wide Stereo's guide doesn't mention it. Crutchfield's .com and .ca pages returned 403, so I couldn't compare against them.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. In a car whose climate controls, factory amp or steering-wheel buttons run through the factory radio, the plan works only with a Maestro-capable receiver plus a module flashed for that vehicle. The Sony XAV-AX6000 (US 'UC' version) qualifies in Sony's own help guide, so it can stay best overall. Without the module, it and ChatGPT's budget picks give no on-screen climate control. Whether the budget picks (Pioneer DMH-1600NEX, Kenwood DMX400S/DMX500S) support Maestro is still unsourced, so the page should not imply they do.

findings.label: Vehicle functions shown through iDatalink Maestro
findings.value: Climate (view status or control the car's climate control), Gauges (speed, engine speed), Vehicle Info (tire pressure, battery voltage), Park Assist (on-screen display for the car's existing parking sensors). Only functions the car supports appear.
findings.source_title: Sony Help Guide XAV-AX6000: Using iDataLink Maestro
findings.note: Section heading is 'iDataLink Maestro (XAV-AX6000(UC))', so this applies to the US/Canada model. Sony says Park Assist is a vision aid only: 'not all obstacles and risks can be detected.'

findings.label: What Maestro setup requires
findings.value: A separately bought iDatalink Maestro module (not included), with firmware installed from idatalinkmaestro.com for your car type and the receiver's serial number. Sony: available functions 'depend on your car type and the firmware'. 'Sony does not guarantee all operations of the iDataLink Maestro functions and settings.'
findings.source_title: Sony Help Guide XAV-AX6000: Getting iDataLink Maestro Ready
findings.note: Steps: find the serial number on the back of the unit or under System > System Information, configure firmware on the Maestro site, then install it to the module. Support contact is Automotive Data Solutions, 1-866-427-2999.

findings.label: iDatalink Maestro RR module: what works with a non-iDatalink stereo, and price
findings.value: 'Basic stereo retention features are available with non-iDataLink compatible stereos'. Listing says the module integrates factory steering-wheel controls and the factory amplifier. $189.99 (list $229.99).
findings.source_title: iDataLink Maestro ADS-MRR Maestro RR Interface Module | Sonic Electronix
findings.note: Retailer listing, not the maker. It does not say which listed features (gauges, climate, parking) need a compatible radio. iDatalink's own site rendered no readable text.

findings.label: What the cited rival already says about Maestro (for comparison)
findings.value: Sony XAV-AX6000, Sony XAV-9000ES, Kenwood DNR1007XR, Kenwood DMX958XR and JVC KW-M795BW: 'Maestro RR/RR2 ready, vehicle dependent'. Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX: 'Maestro RR/RR2 and Metra Axxess, vehicle dependent'. Kenwood KMM-X705: 'no Maestro display integration'. Kenwood DAX1050XR: 'A compatible APX vehicle kit and Maestro hardware are mandatory'.
findings.source_title: Best Car Stereos & Head Units (Tested): 2026 Buyer's Guide - CarAudioNow
findings.note: Rival page that ChatGPT cited. It never mentions CAN bus and doesn't say what Maestro shows on screen or that the module is a separate purchase that must be flashed.
